_doc: Unemployment insurance by state, transcribed from U.S. DOL ETA, Significant Provisions of State Unemployment Insurance Laws, effective July 2026 (https://oui.doleta.gov/unemploy/content/sigpros/2020-2029/July2026.pdf), read 2026-10-20. alts: candidate formulas, the highest wins, each with an optional cap. base: hq = highest quarter wages, avg2 = average of the two highest quarters, sum2 = total of the two highest quarters, bpw = base period wages, q3 = third quarter. mult multiplies the base; add is added. mba: bpwFrac = maximum benefit amount as a share of base period wages (null = no such cap); weeks = [low, high] weeks payable; idx = duration depends on the state unemployment rate; sched = weighted schedule (weeks depend on the BPW/HQW ratio). approx: the formula is a documented simplification of a statutory table.

states.name: Alabama
states.qual: 1½ x HQW
states.mbaText: Lesser of 1/4 BPW or 14 x WBA

states.name: Alaska
states.qual: $2,500; wages in 2 qtrs; at least $250 outside HQ
states.comp: 0.9-2.2% of annual wages + DA up to $72

states.name: Arizona

states.mbaText: 26 x WBA or 24 x WBA if the unemployment rate in the prior calendar qtr is less than 5%

states.name: Arkansas
states.qual: 35 x WBA; wages in 2 qtrs

states.name: North Carolina

states.approx: North Carolina uses the last two quarters of the base period, not the two highest; the engine uses the two highest you enter.
states.mbaText: 12 x WBA
